title: Undenatured type II collagen (UC-II®) for joint support: a randomized ...
abstract:
The study investigated the efficacy and tolerability of UC-II (undenatured type II collagen) in healthy subjects experiencing joint discomfort with physical activity. The study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 55 healthy subjects who reported knee pain after a standardized stepmill performance test. Participants were given either placebo (n=28) or UC-II (40 mg daily, n=27) for 120 days.

Key findings include:
- **Improved Knee Extension:** The UC-II group showed a statistically significant improvement in average knee extension compared to both placebo and baseline after 120 days.
- **Delayed Onset of Pain:** Subjects in the UC-II group exercised longer before experiencing initial joint discomfort at day 120 compared to their baseline.
- **Pain Reduction:** Five individuals in the UC-II group reported no pain during or after the stepmill protocol by the end of the study, compared to one in the placebo group.
- **Tolerability:** No product-related adverse events were observed during the study, indicating UC-II was well-tolerated.

The study concluded that daily supplementation with 40 mg of UC-II improved knee joint extension in healthy subjects and showed potential in lengthening the period of pain-free strenuous exertion and alleviating joint pain associated with such activities.
